ch40.note: 'Crossing into Guandong' (闯关东) names the great migration by which, over the late Qing and Republican years, land-hungry Han from Hebei and Shandong poured across the Shanhaiguan pass into the Northeast—'Guandong' meaning 'east of the pass' (Manchuria). It has nothing to do with the southern province of Guangdong (Canton).

'Enslavement education' (奴化教育) is the standard Chinese term of reproach for the schooling Japan imposed in Manchukuo and Taiwan—education meant to instill loyalty to Japan and wear away the pupils' sense of themselves as Chinese.
A prestigious private university in Tokyo (founded 1882) and a favored destination for the many Chinese who went to study in Japan; the name marks these men as of elite Japanese schooling.

The Long March (1934–35), the roughly year-long fighting retreat of the Communist Red Army from its encircled base in Jiangxi to the northwest of Shaanxi—some 25,000 li, about 12,500 kilometers—which the Party afterward made into its founding epic of endurance.

Zhu De (朱德, 1886–1976), commander-in-chief of the Red Army and its wartime Eighth Route Army, and Peng Dehuai (彭德怀, 1898–1974), his deputy and later the commander of Chinese forces in the Korean War—two of the most senior Communist soldiers.

Miaofengshan, a mountain northwest of Beijing long famous as a pilgrimage site: its spring temple fair, honoring the goddess Bixia Yuanjun, drew crowds of incense-bearing pilgrims from the city, with the pinwheels and hawthorn-strings of the closing passage among its stock delights.
